item.title: Miss Bird of Paradise pageant Northern province- set for November
item.description: Prominent young women in Northern Province are gearing up to host the first of its kind Miss Bird of Paradise Northern Province Pageant in November 2026. Deputy Chairlady of Miss MBOP Northern Province 2026, Ms Kewana Inurapa, said the quest is the first of its kind that will be hosted in the province.
item.content:encoded:
Prominent young women in Northern Province are gearing up to host the first of its kind Miss Bird of Paradise Northern Province Pageant in November 2026.

Deputy Chairlady of Miss MBOP Northern Province 2026, Ms Kewana Inurapa, said the quest is the first of its kind that will be hosted in the province.

Ms Inurapa said six (6) contestants have already been confirmed to participate.

The Organizing Committee of the MBOP Northern Province has started its awareness program to high and secondary schools, including TVET schools in the province.

Ms Inurapa pointed out that the school awareness program is to make known to school-aged women to participate in such upcoming pageants in the future.

"Pageants are events where young women and girls have the opportunity to showcase their beauty and not only that, but the event goes beyond by exposing talents, networking, scholarship programs and employment opportunities," she said.

The upcoming MBOP Northern Province Pageant will be staged in the first week of November 2026.

The six contestants are all university students who will each represent selected LLGs, including Tamata, Higaturu, Tufi, Popondetta Urban, and Kokoda LLG respectively.

Meanwhile, Ms Inurapa said the MBOP Northern Province will be hosting its major Gala Fundraising Dinner in Port Moresby to raise funds towards the event.

She called on Northern people living in Port Moresby to come along and support the fundraising drive.

Ms Inurapa also said the Patron for the MBOP Northern Province 2026 is Northern Governor, Hon. Gary Juffa.

item.title: Brugam secondary in remote Maprik graduates 508 students
item.description: Brugam Secondary school, a South Sea Evangelical Church (SSEC) institution in the remote Bumbita-Muhian Local Level Government area of Maprik District, has graduated 508 students. The school held its 21st Grade 10 and 15th Grade 12 graduation on 1st October under the theme “Shine Through Discipline”, with 230 Grade 10 and 278 Grade 12 students graduating.
item.content:encoded:
Brugam Secondary school, a South Sea Evangelical Church (SSEC) institution in the remote Bumbita-Muhian Local Level Government area of Maprik District, has graduated 508 students.

The school held its 21st Grade 10 and 15th Grade 12 graduation on 1st October under the theme “Shine Through Discipline”, with 230 Grade 10 and 278 Grade 12 students graduating.

Located about 30 kilometres west of Maprik town, Brugam Secondary serves students from different districts across East Sepik Province, reflecting the South Sea Evangelical Church's commitment to providing education to communities beyond its immediate location.

Presenting the school's report, Principal Aminson Kundun acknowledged the continued support from the Maprik District Development Authority, Ambunti-Dreikikier District Development Authority and the Office of East Sepik Governor Allan Bird.

Kundun said the support had contributed to the development of the school, which caters for students from across the province and not only Maprik District.

Reflecting on what makes Brugam students unique, Kundun highlighted their determination to pursue their goals despite challenges after completing secondary education.

“Not all students who graduate from Brugam Secondary find spaces in tertiary institutions, but one thing that makes them stand out from the rest is that they don’t give up. They always work hard, find another way around and achieve their dreams,” Kundun said.

East Sepik Governor Allan Bird, who attended the graduation, delivered the keynote address and encouraged the graduates to continue learning.

“I don’t want you to stop learning. I am happy with the words of your principal. Even if you don’t make it, your grades are not good, use every opportunity to learn,” Governor Bird said.

He reminded the graduates that education was important whether they pursued professional careers or returned to their communities to work on their land.

“Whether you want to become a doctor or pilot, or want to go back and look after your land in your community, in both cases you need to be educated,” he said.

Governor Bird also challenged the graduates to look beyond their villages and province, saying education could open opportunities around the world.

“Don’t just aim for the country. Aim for the world. Education gives you the ticket to see the world. Don’t limit yourself to your village, province and country. The world is out there,” he said.

Meanwhile, South Sea Evangelical Church Education Secretary and Brugam Secondary School Board of Governors Chairman Mack Yarbange acknowledged Governor Bird's presence, saying it added value to the graduation and recognition of the students.

item.title: PNG to host 9th Pacific Media Summit in 2028
item.description: Papua New Guinea is set to host the 9th Pacific Islands News Association (PINA) Media Summit in Port Moresby in 2028. The Media Council of PNG (MCPNG) and the National Broadcasting Corporation of Papua New Guinea (NBC PNG) have jointly put forward a bid to host the regional summit.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea is set to host the 9th Pacific Islands News Association (PINA) Media Summit in Port Moresby in 2028.

The Media Council of PNG (MCPNG) and the National Broadcasting Corporation of Papua New Guinea (NBC PNG) have jointly put forward a bid to host the regional summit.

Speaking at the 8th Pacific Media Summit in Fiji recently, President of the PNG Media Council and newly appointed PINA President Neville Choi said the bid comes at an important time for the country and the Pacific media industry.

Choi said PNG wants to use its experience in working with government and the media industry to contribute to discussions across the Pacific.

“We are ready to host. And we have a very, very tough act to follow. I think the Fiji Media Association has shown that this is the level and standard of a PINA summit that we want to be.”

President Choi added that PNG's media industry has strengthened its relationship with government over the past three to four years, while continuing to push for self-regulation.

There are also concerns about possible changes in government and leadership following PNG's next general election, expected in 2027.

Choi stressed that the Media industry in PNG wants to build on the progress already made before those political changes take place.

He said PNG's experience could also provide lessons for smaller Pacific countries dealing with similar challenges around media regulation, press freedom and government relations.

PNG's cultural diversity, with more than a thousand tribes, was also highlighted as one of the country's strengths in bringing different voices together.

The joint bid also comes as the Pacific media industry faces growing challenges from misinformation, technology and pressure on press freedom.

Choi representing PNG acknowledged the high standard set by Fiji in hosting the 8th PINA summit, but said PNG is ready for the challenge.

“It’s going to be, like I said, a tough act to follow, but we are up to the challenge. And if you are all supportive, then we want you along with us on this," Choi said.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Solomon Islands Broadcasting Corporation (SIBC) Johnson Honimae seconded MCPNG AND NBC PNG's bid and move the motion in favour of PNG to host the 2028 9th PINA Media Summit in Port Moresby, PNG.

"This AGM, I want to support and move the bid from PNG Media Council and NBC PNG to host the 2028 PINA Summit".

item.title: Planning Secretary Konny Samuel ends 27-year public service career
item.description: Planning Secretary Koney Samuel has stepped down from office after 27 years of service to the Government and people of Papua New Guinea. Mr Samuel, 51, served as Secretary for the Department of National Planning and Monitoring for eight years.
item.content:encoded:
Planning Secretary Koney Samuel has stepped down from office after 27 years of service to the Government and people of Papua New Guinea.

Mr Samuel, 51, served as Secretary for the Department of National Planning and Monitoring for eight years.

He became Acting Secretary in July 2018 and was later appointed Secretary in May 2019. He served two consecutive terms before stepping down in October 2026.

Mr Samuel said he was leaving for personal reasons and believed it was time to give younger leaders an opportunity to serve.

“My decision to leave office stems from personal reasons. When I first took office as Secretary 2018, I was ready to take on the challenges of my new role, and I am proud of what we have achieved together over the years,” Mr Samuel said.

During his time as Secretary, Mr Samuel helped lead important national planning and development work.

This included seven Capital Investment Budgets, the Medium Term Development Plans III and IV, improvements to public investment management, PNG’s Second Voluntary National Review on the Sustainable Development Goals, and stronger partnerships with development partners.

He also supported reforms in infrastructure and the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene sector.

Mr Samuel thanked the Planning Ministers he worked with, including Richard Maru, the late Sam Basil, Renbo Paita and current Minister Sir Ano Pala.

He also thanked public servants, development partners, stakeholders and his family for their support.

“I believe the time is right for me to step aside and give opportunity to the younger generation of leaders to rise and take charge. I have served my country and people to the best of my ability, and I leave office with gratitude for the opportunity I have been given to serve,” Mr Samuel said.

He also thanked the Marape-Rosso Government for giving him the opportunity to serve as Secretary and thanked God for his strength and guidance during his 27 years of public service.

Meanwhile, the National Executive Council met on September 30 and appointed DNPM Deputy Secretary for Programming and Monitoring, Roger Kara, as Acting Secretary for the department.

item.title: PNG-Fiji Business Council aims to help SMEs enter new markets
item.description: The newly established Papua New Guinea-Fiji Business Council will help small businesses in PNG and Fiji find new markets, business partners and opportunities in both countries. The council held its first membership event at the Hilton Hotel in Port Moresby last night.
item.content:encoded:
The newly established Papua New Guinea-Fiji Business Council will help small businesses in PNG and Fiji find new markets, business partners and opportunities in both countries.

The council held its first membership event at the Hilton Hotel in Port Moresby last night.

Sir Mahesh Patel, OBE, founder and Chairman Emeritus of CPL Group, said the idea came after discussions with the Fiji High Commission and Fiji's Deputy Prime Minister during his visit to PNG.

He said the main purpose of the council was to connect businesses from the two countries.

“The idea was to ask how we can encourage businesses to talk to each other,” Sir Mahesh said.

He said many small businesses in PNG wanted to enter the Fiji market but did not know where to start.

“There's a lot of SMEs that we support through CPL. They always say, How can we enter the Fiji market, or how can we get business from there?" he said.

Sir Mahesh said the council would create a database of businesses in PNG and Fiji.

“We don't want to have conferences and meetings. We want to create a database so if a person wants to do business in Fiji, or from Fiji to Papua New Guinea, they can say, ‘I'm in this industry, can I go and talk to that person?" he said.

“Our council will be there to network with the people and connect the people. That's the main aim.”

Sir Mahesh emphasised that the main focus of the council would be small and medium-sized businesses.

“I think my target is the SMEs. Corporates can find out where to go. The SMEs should try and contact us,” he said.

He said large companies usually had the money and resources to find new markets, but small businesses often needed help.

“Big corporates can go their own ways and expand businesses, but it's only those small businesses that find it difficult to reach the market that will be assisted through this council,” he said.

He encouraged SMEs with business ideas to contact the council.

“If they want to have business ideas, if they want to go to Fiji, contact us and let's see if we can help them. Our aim is to be the bridge between the two countries,” he said.

Meanwhile, Sir Mahesh said there were many opportunities for PNG businesses to sell their products in Fiji.

He pointed to agriculture as one example.

“People in Fiji say, when they come to visit Papua New Guinea, our fruits and vegetables are so good. They say, ‘How can we export?’ So again, there's a market there,” he said.

However, he said businesses would need to work together to collect products and arrange transport and cold storage.

“It's a long process. We need transportation, cold storage,” he said.

He also pointed to young PNG entrepreneurs making skincare and hair products.

“There's a lot of young people now developing skincare or hair products in Papua New Guinea. So how can we sell that to Fiji to stop them importing it?” he said.

The president of the council and Chief Operating Officer of MRDC Vele Rupa said the establishment of the council was an important step for both countries.

“This is a huge step ahead, not only for the two nations in business, but most importantly in strengthening the existing relationship,” he said.

Sir Mahesh said the council was only starting its journey, but he believed it could make a difference for small businesses in both countries.

“The journey is long, but we're starting something and it will definitely go a long way in helping the little people from both countries,” he said.

Meanwhile, the PNG-Fiji Business Council was established in April 2026. It is open to businesses of different sizes and industries in PNG and Fiji.

The council hopes to help businesses from both countries connect, share ideas, form partnerships and find new markets.

item.title: September 16 murder suspects detained in Goroka
item.description: Two main suspects who were allegedly involved in the murder of Marot Keteno on September 16, 2026 have been arrested and are now detained at the at Goroka Police Station. Eastern Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent, Albert Beli has confirmed the two suspects and they will be charged accordingly.
item.content:encoded:
Two main suspects who were allegedly involved in the murder of Marot Keteno on September 16, 2026 have been arrested and are now detained at the at Goroka Police Station.

Eastern Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent, Albert Beli has confirmed the two suspects and they will be charged accordingly.

​PPC Beli, while acknowledging the good work that his officers have done, is also calling on the relatives of the deceased not to take the law into their own hands, as the matter is now in police hands.

​"I am calling on the family members of the late deceased to assist the police instead of taking the law into their own hands.

“A wrong has been done, and we must let the law take its course. We must not create another wrong because that will not fix what has happened; it will only lead to bigger problems," PPC Beli said.

​PPC Beli further thanked the police officers and community leaders who assisted in bringing forward the main suspects under investigation. He said the two will remain in police custody and will appear in court as soon as their court files are ready.

item.title: Madang women crowned queens of Northern Region PNGFA Cup
item.description: The Madang Soccer Association (MSA) women’s team has been crowned champions of the 2026 Northern Region PNG Football Association (PNGFA) Cup Qualifiers after defeating Lae Football Association (LFA) 1–0 in the grand final at Laiwaden Oval in Madang. MSA scored the only goal of the match in the 20th minute of the first half to take the lead.
item.content:encoded:
The Madang Soccer Association (MSA) women’s team has been crowned champions of the 2026 Northern Region PNG Football Association (PNGFA) Cup Qualifiers after defeating Lae Football Association (LFA) 1–0 in the grand final at Laiwaden Oval in Madang.

MSA scored the only goal of the match in the 20th minute of the first half to take the lead.

Lae Football Association made several attempts to find an equaliser, but Madang’s defence held firm until the final hooter to secure the championship victory.

The MSA women’s head coach, Tracey Kig, praised her players for their performance and commitment throughout the tournament.

“The girls played really well. With our support and guidance, they played the way we wanted them to.

“Keep the ball and build up to score,”she said.

She said the team would now focus on improving their fitness, strength, and combination play ahead of the next stage of the competition.

“We need to work on our fitness and strength, and also our combination, to get ready for the second leg in Lae next month,” she said.

“I give credit to my girls for their time and effort in training. They deserve this win.”

LFA finished second in the women’s division, while Wewak defeated Wau 1–0 to secure third place, with Wau finishing fourth.

In the men’s division, Wau defeated Morobe Football Association (MFA) 1–0 to claim first place in the Northern Region PNGFA Cup Qualifier. Morobe finished runners-up.

Madang Soccer Association defeated Lae Football Association 3–2 in the third-place playoff to finish third, while LFA finished fourth.

Madang Soccer Association president and PNGFA vice-president responsible for the Northern Region, Siegfried Beschel, thanked all participating teams, saying the tournament demonstrated the true spirit of unity through sport.

Beschel said football has a strong following across the Momase region and called for greater recognition and support for the sport.

“Rugby is not the national sport, especially for the Momase region.

“In the Northern Region, we are soccer-loving people. We need to let our government know that Momase are soccer-loving people.” he said.

He also acknowledged the associate and affiliate members who travelled from outside Madang, particularly the Wewak teams, to participate in the tournament.

“To travel is always expensive, so we need support from the government and local MPs to support us to promote soccer in the region,” he said.

MSA and LFA women’s teams , Wau and MFA mean's team will now advance to the next stage of the PNGFA Cup, which will be held in Lae in November.

Wewak will host the 2027 Northern Region PNGFA Cup Qualifiers.

item.title: 50-Year sentences for homemade gun manufacturers in Hela
item.description: The ongoing illegal firearm surrender program across the Tari-Pori District of Hela Province has successfully yielded. Hela Governor Philip Undialu said nearly 500 homemade firearms have been surrendered across three Local Level Governments
item.content:encoded:
The ongoing illegal firearm surrender program across the Tari-Pori District of Hela Province has successfully yielded.

Hela Governor Philip Undialu said nearly 500 homemade firearms have been surrendered across three Local Level Governments

​During the third official gun surrender event for the Hayapuga LLG, held at Hiwanda Primary School, Governor Undialu issued a stern command to local covert gunsmiths, demanding an immediate end to the production of illegal weapons. He urged communities to report directly to law enforcement.

​"Under Section 21 of Papua New Guinea's Counter-Terrorism Act 2024, individuals implicated in manufacturing firearms face up to 50 years in prison," he said.

He made it clear that tribal warfare, murder, and weapon fabrication are now legally classified as acts of terrorism, stripping warlords of local status and marking them explicitly as criminals.

​The Governor noted that while individuals handing over weapons displayed genuine remorse and a commitment to reform, local arms manufacturers threaten to undermine peace by dragging former combatants back into violent conflict.

He said those involved in past tribal fights and have surrendered their weapons are encouraged to actively join church ministries to aid their transition into civilian life, backed by coordinated assistance from government bodies, non-governmental organizations, and community leaders.

​“The Marape-Rosso Government will provide Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) funding support specifically for individuals who surrender military-grade or high-powered weapons,” he said.

​Governor Undialu stressed that his focus will now shift heavily toward expanding education, fostering SME growth, and advancing agriculture activities.
